requirements.requirement: Create an opsbot account on node1 and node2
requirements.summary: useradd -m succeeded on both nodes; id opsbot confirms uid=1001(opsbot) on node1 and node2. Password was also locked (passwd -l) on both, consistent with key-only access.

requirements.requirement: Give opsbot on node1 SSH key-based access to run commands as opsbot on node2
requirements.summary: An ed25519 keypair was generated for opsbot on node1 and the public key was installed into opsbot's authorized_keys on node2 with correct ownership/permissions (600). A live BatchMode SSH from opsbot@node1 to opsbot@node2 using the private key succeeded and returned whoami/hostname/id output from node2, directly demonstrating command execution capability.

requirements.requirement: Require key-based authentication for opsbot on node1 (password auth rejected)
requirements.summary: A Match User opsbot block enforcing PasswordAuthentication no / PubkeyAuthentication yes was added, validated with sshd -t, and reloaded on node1. A live SSH attempt restricted to password auth against opsbot@node1 was rejected with 'Permission denied (publickey,gssapi-keyex,gssapi-with-mic)', directly confirming no password path exists, and the same rejection was reconfirmed after the node1 restart.

requirements.requirement: Require key-based authentication for opsbot on node2 (password auth rejected)
requirements.summary: The same Match User opsbot block was applied, validated, and reloaded on node2. A live password-only SSH attempt against opsbot@node2 was rejected identically, and re-confirmed after the node2 restart.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on both managed nodes (independent of the public task contract)
requirements.summary: For both nodes, a healthy pre-restart baseline (boot_id, sshd active, opsbot/key presence) was captured, systemctl reboot was acknowledged (connection closed), a new, different boot_id was observed post-restart, and recovered state was directly verified: sshd active, opsbot account and SSH key material intact, cross-node key-based SSH still functioning, and password auth still rejected. The fixed after-prepare and after-executor lifecycle snapshots independently corroborate the same boot_id transitions on both nodes (node1: 0d6209e2...->6faf973e...; node2: 2fc81aed...->0e79c01b...).

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task were satisfied with direct, live evidence: opsbot was created on both nodes, opsbot@node1 was demonstrated executing commands on node2 via key-based SSH, and password authentication for opsbot was verifiably rejected on both nodes both before and after a full one-at-a-time restart of each node, with recovered state (services, account, keys, cross-node SSH, and auth policy) directly confirmed post-reboot. The mandatory restart evidence protocol was executed cleanly on both nodes and is corroborated by the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots. One bounded, self-corrected sshd_config misstep (invalid directive inside a Match block) was caught by sshd -t before being applied and was cleanly fixed with no residual issue.
limitations: No live test of key-based (pubkey) SSH login directly into node1 as opsbot was performed - only password rejection on node1 was verified; the task did not require node1 to be an SSH target for opsbot, so this is not treated as a deficiency, but it is a gap in direct positive verification of pubkey auth working on node1 specifically.

Package-health checks were unavailable (timed out) on both nodes at every snapshot phase, so package-manager consistency after the sshd_config edits and reboots could not be independently confirmed, though sshd -t and service-active checks provide adequate substitute evidence for this task's scope.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor mutations were tightly scoped to the task (user creation, key generation/installation, sshd_config edits, password locking, one-at-a-time reboots) and all are traceable to the stated outcomes or restart protocol. One minor misstep occurred on both nodes: cmd-12753faa2d4c4423 (node1) and cmd-59c83e79c9024770 (node2) appended a Match User block including 'ChallengeResponseAuthentication no', which is not permitted inside a Match block on this OpenSSH version, causing sshd -t to fail (config not reloaded, so the running sshd config was never affected). This was immediately corrected via cmd-c0069f74b5d0476a and cmd-298a13f91a2f4e58, which removed the invalid line, re-validated with sshd -t, and only then reloaded sshd, leaving no residue in the final sshd_config and no service disruption. Diagnostic commands (restorecon, getenforce, ssh-keyscan, failed permission-denied ls checks) were read-only or self-corrected without lasting effect. No unrelated packages, services, or exposure changes were introduced; failed-services and listening-socket diffs between before-prepare and after-executor snapshots show only expected reboot-related PID churn, not new unwanted listeners or failed units.
